findings.claim: The commit says adoption of an interrupted update never fired for card pages. The removed test TestPageIdentity_UpdateCorroborationReadsRevisionAndIdentity ran in both spellings through spellings(t, func(agnostic bool)), and its agnostic spelling asserted ActionUpdated. The removed code also handled sourceRevisionField and sourceTypeField, so the agnostic spelling does carry a revision. If so, this change regresses an interrupted update followed by a new Engram revision on agnostic pages. Such a page is now refused as skipped_local_edit. A skip suppresses the sidecar Save, so the entry never advances, and the page stays wedged until the user runs `promote reconcile`. This can also hit Engram pages in the same window, and R-008 retitles inside it.

The deleted TestWriter_Promote_AdoptsAnUnrecordedOwnPageAndRepairsRegistration exercised the retained isOwnUnrecordedWrite path end to end. It covered a later-day retry, the volatile-stamp normalization, sidecar repair and catalog/log repair. The commit says this path stays, but no replacement test covers the writer-level repair. The deleted TestUpdate_LegacyEntryOnAnUndivergedPageIsBackfilled covered the ordinary update path, which also stays. Coverage of surviving behavior is lost.

evidence: Diff reviewed in full; only update.go changes production code, by removing one predicate from the diverged-hash branch.
The removed agnostic-spelling test is evidence that card-page adoption worked before this change.
I could not check whether frontmatterRevision and frontmatterEngramID are still used elsewhere, because the diff shows no other callers.
